source_snapshot.items: All SSD NVMe LED Check - Access /Busy
source_snapshot.procedure: Insert an NVMe SSD into the backplane slot and check that the Access/Busy LED works normally; collect photos and inspect system logs.
source_snapshot.criteria: Check the LED function defined by the system specification.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL retains operator observation but suggests locate-style controller/BMC commands and undocumented raw IPMI, which do not create or prove real storage activity.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: RPUC/CHANGED with HIGH storage/data/control risk; define idle and active states, an identity-locked data-safe I/O stimulus, operator photos and complete storage evidence.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Recognizes the visual limitation but does not distinguish Access/Busy activity indication from a Locate/UID control path.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Requires a bounded approved workload on the exact SSD and physical observation before, during and after I/O.
historical_reviews.related_cases: Row81 validates passive presence and row83 validates explicit Locate/UID control; this case alone requires real device activity and return to idle.
historical_reviews.v3_1: The I/O source, LED transitions and stable drive-slot identity must share timestamps so background RAID or another disk cannot create a false observation.

original_test_intent: Verify that each approved NVMe backplane slot displays the specified Access/Busy LED behavior for the mapped SSD during controlled storage activity and returns to its defined idle state afterward.
original_method: A qualified operator inserts and watches the mapped SSD while the agent applies only an approved read-only or isolated test-file workload to that exact stable device, recording synchronized I/O, LED, storage-health and log evidence.
manual_activity: User approves the workload and data boundary; qualified operator inserts the SSD and photographs the Access/Busy LED at idle, during I/O and after stop; agent controls only the approved workload and evidence capture.
required_inputs: Stable SSD/NVMe ID to slot/backplane/controller mapping
Access/Busy LED state, color, cadence and response/settle timing specification
Read-only device or isolated test-file workload, rate and duration
Qualified operator, OOB/console and protected evidence location
safety_requirements: Resolve the workload target by stable identity and exclude boot, EFI, swap, mounted production, RAID member and unknown devices from raw writes
Prefer a read-only or approved disposable-file workload and record exact start/stop timestamps
Do not clear existing system or SEL evidence
Stop on wrong target, unexpected write, I/O/RAID/filesystem/thermal/SEL error, access loss or anomalous LED state
Do not use Locate/UID or undocumented raw IPMI as a substitute for activity
agent_execution_scope: Capture idle baseline, start and stop the exact approved workload, and record I/O counters for the target only
Collect stable enumeration, mount/RAID/NVMe health and complete logs before/during/after activity
Correlate operator photos to workload timestamps and verify the post-I/O idle transition
Do not observe the physical LED remotely, select an unsafe target, rebuild/recover or issue verdict
engineer_actions: Approve the exact workload, target, LED transition and data/recovery contract
Provide a qualified operator and validate physical observation coverage
Review synchronized LED/I/O/health evidence and decide PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The enumeration portion may assist, but a locate or generic raw LED command neither generates ordinary NVMe access nor proves Access/Busy behavior; insecure SSH and unscoped control are unacceptable.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Run only the approved identity-bound read-only or disposable-file I/O workload with synchronized device counters, NVMe/RAID health and complete logs; no generic raw/locate command belongs in the acceptance path.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: NVMe insertion, Access/Busy LED observation and the source 15/8 timing fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Capture a three-phase idle/activity/recovery observation for every mapped SSD, tying physical LED video or photos to target-specific I/O telemetry.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Defines the actual activity stimulus, data boundary, timestamps and recovery evidence needed to distinguish the tested drive from background activity.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Automation supplies controlled I/O and telemetry but the operator remains authoritative for the physical indicator.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Background RAID or filesystem activity can illuminate the LED independently; target counters and synchronized observation are needed to avoid false correlation.

project_override_considerations: Controller caching, enclosure aggregation or a combined status/activity LED may change expected cadence; the platform specification must define the observable state and settle interval for each slot.
expected_evidence: Operator/date and timestamped idle, active and post-stop photos or video
Exact workload command, target stable ID, PID, duration, exit status and I/O counters
Complete mount/RAID/NVMe/SMART/temperature state before and after
Workload cleanup, final population/restoration and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The sources agree on an Access/Busy LED visual check; GPT V2 correctly distinguishes the required activity workload from DeepSeek's non-equivalent locate/raw-control suggestion.

blocked_analysis.analysis: An approved workload, LED specification and operator are normal execution prerequisites; the purpose and safe review boundaries are clear.

review_improvement: Replaces the locate-command shortcut with synchronized real I/O, target-specific telemetry and physical observation across idle, busy and recovery phases.
independent_technical_reasoning: An Access/Busy LED is driven by actual device or enclosure activity, so a software indicator-control command tests a different path. Because background RAID work and controller caching can create or suppress apparent blinking, acceptance requires a bounded workload on the exact stable SSD plus synchronized counters and operator-visible transitions before, during and after that workload.
